jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Selective Survival
jokes.joke: After the apocalypse, I found the last nightclub on Earth. The bouncer looked at my torn clothes, homemade spear, and three days of radioactive dust and said, “Not with those shoes.” I said, “Humanity is down to twelve people.” He checked the clipboard: “Exactly. We can finally be selective.”

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Bouncer Apocalypse
jokes.joke: After the apocalypse I became a bouncer for the last nightclub on Earth. It's not hard. There's a list, there's two names on it, and one of them is a guy named Gary who's been dead since Tuesday. Still, I stand there all night, arms crossed, going 'not tonight' to zombies. They don't even want in. They just miss having somewhere to be turned away from.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Wasteland Logistics
jokes.joke: I'm not worried about ruthless motorcycle gangs taking over in a post-apocalyptic wasteland, because my friend group is way too disorganized for that. I can't even get four of them to agree on a time for Sunday brunch. You really think we're going to successfully coordinate a fifty-car convoy to raid a desert fortress? We'd be ten miles down Fury Road and I'd have to pull the war rig over because Dave forgot his spiked shoulder pads.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Door Policy
jokes.joke: I work as a bouncer in the post-apocalypse. It's the only job left that still has a working door. Last night a guy covered in radiation scars and wearing a traffic cone walks up. I say, "You're not on the list." He stares at me and goes, "There is no list. There is no society." I looked him over and said, "Then the cover charge is two cans of beans and whatever's left of your dignity."

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Calm Night
jokes.joke: I once worked as a bouncer, which was a terrible fit because I don’t really do anger. One guy tried to start a fight, and instead of throwing him out, I calmly told him, “Sir, I am extremely disappointed in your choices.” He froze like I’d hit him with dad energy. That was the first time anyone backed down because I sounded like a report card.

scores.comment: Strong premise, clean escalation, and a distinctive final turn that gives the zombies an unexpectedly human motive.
Clear and relatable with good visual specificity, but the disorganized-friends-versus-apocalypse contrast follows a familiar route.
Several solid lines and a coherent setting, though the dignity tag is less sharp than the working-door setup.
The report-card comparison lands mildly, but the narrator explicitly retains composure rather than losing it, so only one seed concept is clearly used.
Clean setup/turn, standard 'exclusive club' joke shape but well executed and snappy.
Solid relatable premise, Mad Max riff funny but runs a bit long before the Dave payoff.
Competent bouncer bit but 'cover charge' turn is fairly predictable and a touch flat.
Fresh angle on a bouncer joke, 'dad energy' and 'report card' land as a genuine surprise turn.
Solid, classic setup-punchline structure with a crisp final beat. The nightclub/shoes trope in an apocalypse is slightly predictable, but the execution and timing land well.
Great stage rhythm and subtle observational humor. The bit about zombies missing having somewhere to be turned away from gives it a strong, memorable tag line.
Functional stand-up premise, but the ending fizzles slightly by trailing off into a generic 'beans and dignity' joke rather than a sharp turn.
Relatable premise with natural conversational flow. The 'dad energy' comparison works, though the final phrase leans a bit conventional.
Clean setup and selective payoff land as mild amusement; turn is competent but expected.
Solid stage voice and zombies-missing-rejection finish give a genuine comic snap.
Specific brunch-to-Fury-Road escalation works; concrete and repeatable.
Gentle-disappointment angle is clear but mild and familiar; report-card line only softens.
Clean premise with a neat turn; solid but not standout.
Fun imagery but the escalation repeats; mild payoff.
Strong relatable angle with a clear, funny turn.
Good imagery and a clean final line; respectable overall.
